chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into ihram for Hajj and Umrah together, then arrived in Mecca while the people were at Arafat. He feared that if he performed Tawaf and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, he would miss the standing (at Arafat). He said: 'He should leave the Umrah, and when he completes his Hajj, he should do as Aisha did, and there is no sacrifice (Hady) upon him.'

key_terms.إِهْلَال: Entering into the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills in Mecca)
key_terms.سَعَى: Performed Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.عَائِشَةُ: Aisha (wife of the Prophet, known for her Hajj practice)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the site of the essential standing during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if combining Hajj and Umrah causes him to miss the standing at Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical dilemma of a pilgrim practicing *Qiran* (combining Hajj and Umrah) who risks missing the critical standing at Arafat while performing Umrah rituals. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that he should defer the Umrah to after Hajj, mirroring the precedent of Aisha (RA), and exempts him from the *hady* (sacrifice) typically required for *Qiran*, highlighting the Shia emphasis on preserving the pillar of Arafat over ritual completeness. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence to prioritize essential acts (*rukn*) when time is constrained.
